On this page

Agents & Departments ​

Saidi has two kinds of agent, and one grouping construct.

Project agents ​

A project agent is bound to a registered repo. It works in that repo's checkout, on that repo's branch, under that project's policy (branch, approval, verify — see Project Policy).

It runs in one of two modes:

  • ask — read-only investigation. Tool set is Read, Grep, Glob.
  • work — makes changes, commits them, and (under branch: new) opens a PR.

Project agents are addressed by their registry name, which is also what appears as a checklist task's assignee.

Custom agents ​

Custom agents are the non-repo specialists — Finance, Research, Ops, a CRM operator. They live under agents/<name>/ with:

FilePurpose
AGENT.mdPersona prompt, plus optional frontmatter
skills/Claude plugin skills
agents/Nested sub-agents
hooks/Lifecycle hooks
.mcp.jsonMCP servers this agent may reach

They use the same spawn machinery as project agents, rooted at the agent's configured cwd.

ts
interface CustomAgent {
  name: string;
  dir: string;
  cwd: string;
  description: string;
  prompt: string;
  department: string;
  lead: boolean;
  model?: string;
  profile?: string;       // provider profile ('' = inherit)
  effort?: EffortMode;    // '' = inherit run-wide / global
  permission: 'all' | 'read-only' | 'custom';
  tools: string[];        // exact allow-list when permission is 'custom'
}

Permissions ​

permissionTool set
all (default)Every tool
read-onlyRead, Grep, Glob — named explicitly, not inferred
customExactly the tools: list

Enforcement is layered: the SDK is handed a restricted tool set, and a canUseTool gate sits behind it. Set this in AGENT.md frontmatter, or via Settings → Permissions.

Departments ​

A department is a string on the agent (department: Development). Agents that share one form a team. One of them may be the lead (lead: true).

A lead is not just a label — it changes what toolbelt the agent is spawned with:

  • A department lead gets its own delegate_to_project tool, scoped to that department's projects. The lead routes work down to the repo agents rather than doing it itself.
  • A lead with team members gets delegate_to_specialist and delegate_to_specialists (the parallel form), scoped to the other agents in its department, plus a prompt fragment naming its team.
  • A non-lead specialist gets no delegation tools. It does the work.

So the shape you build is a small org chart: PRIME → department lead → project or specialist agent.

Provider, model, and effort resolution ​

Every actor resolves its execution settings through a most-specific-wins chain:

per-agent-in-run override (Run.agentConfigs[actor])
  → run-wide override (Run.model / Run.providerProfile / Run.effortMode)
    → the agent's own default (CustomAgent.model / profile / effort)
      → the global default (Settings)

An empty string or an absent field means inherit, not override with nothing.

Managing agents ​

ToolDoes
list_agentsLists custom agents with department, lead flag, permission
create_agentCreates agents/<name>/AGENT.md with persona and frontmatter
remove_agentDeletes the agent directory
add_skillWrites a skill into agents/<name>/skills/
import_skillFetches a skill from a URL
add_mcp_server / remove_mcp_serverEdits the agent's .mcp.json

See also: Delegation · Writing a Custom Agent
